prayerExcerpt.en-US: "Lay not up to yourselves treasures on earth, but in heaven, where neither rust nor moth doth consume."
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: "Não ajunteis para vós tesouros na terra, mas no céu, onde nem a ferrugem nem a traça os consomem."

meta.face: A Greek noblewoman of about forty with a pale, ivory complexion and a SQUARE-OVAL face with a BROAD, STRAIGHT JAW — a smooth, broad forehead, a straight nose with a slight AQUILINE bump high on the bridge, VERY LARGE, dark, DEEP-SET, luminous eyes under THICK, dark brows that nearly MEET over the nose, cheeks a little thinned by fasting, a FULL, closed mouth, a firm, rounded chin; dark hair hidden under the veil but for a parting; the look calm and self-possessed. Not the old, heart-shaped marcella, the round, full bathildes, the short, wide radegundes, the lean, droop-eyed clotilda helena (long face, Roman nose) or the young, full-oval, light-eyed barbara.
meta.basis: No likeness survives. The large, dark eyes and heavy brows follow the icon on English Wikipedia, as a Byzantine woman of rank; the age follows Wikipedia (born about 365, died 408). The altar linen is the book's ('the duties of which were to prepare the altar linen'); the plain dress follows her giving her fortune to the poor. St. John Chrysostom is left off.
